sections.title: See the safety boundary before giving an agent work

steps.title: Understand the governed loop
steps.description: Learn where model reasoning ends and specifications, permissions, reviews, and evidence begin.
steps.completion: You can name which decisions belong to the model and which must remain explicit and inspectable.

steps.title: Review plugin trust and scope
steps.description: Inspect what an Agent Plugin can instruct Claude to do before installing it.
steps.completion: You know which instructions will enter the session and which authority they do not grant.

sections.title: Build the source-owned plan and specification

steps.title: Install the focused plugins
steps.description: Follow the Agent Plugins installation contract for Claude Code.
steps.completion: Claude can discover the selected beyond10x plugin instructions.

steps.title: Build the governed first plan
steps.description: Use the repository-owned golden path to adopt, model, decompose, scope, run critics, and preserve the unresolved decision instead of guessing it.
steps.completion: The ESS model and planning store validate, scopes retain their citations, critic verdicts are recorded, and the open decision blocker remains inspectable.

steps.title: Project the specification into documentation
steps.description: Use ESS to generate deterministic human-readable documentation from the validated system specification.
steps.completion: Re-running generation from unchanged inputs produces unchanged documentation bytes.

sections.title: Inspect the proof, then decide whether to implement

steps.title: Inspect the evidence trail
steps.description: Check that claims about the work point to concrete outputs rather than a fluent transcript.
steps.completion: You can distinguish a claimed result from evidence that another person or tool can verify.

steps.title: Choose whether to attempt implementation
steps.description: Treat the golden path's implementation wave and reference driver as optional experimental follow-ons: the published driven run does not reach completion today.
steps.completion: You have made an explicit go or no-go decision; completing this planning path does not depend on launching or finishing a driven implementation.

steps.title: Learn the safe coding loop
steps.description: See why a useful autonomous coding loop separates intent, execution, review, evidence, and authority.
steps.completion: You can identify the five boundaries in an agentic coding task.

steps.title: Follow the deeper architecture narrative
steps.description: Read how evidence-backed principles connect to deterministic mechanisms and governed reach.
steps.completion: You understand the conceptual stack without treating it as one mandatory dependency chain.

sections.title: Inspect the boundaries in their owning documentation

steps.title: See how work becomes governed
steps.description: Use AEP's overview to inspect typed work, gates, and evidence.
steps.completion: You can identify the work decision that AEP makes explicit.

steps.title: See how system intent becomes executable
steps.description: Use ESS's overview to distinguish specifications from generated documentation and contracts.
steps.completion: You can describe specification-to-document generation without claiming that prose is ESS input.

steps.title: See how an agent loop stays observable
steps.description: Inspect the Harness model for tools, approvals, effects, budgets, and retained sessions.
steps.completion: You can name the evidence a native agent run should retain.

steps.title: Choose an entry point by outcome
steps.description: Decide whether your next action is to try a governed change, build an agent system, or evaluate a product.
steps.completion: You can choose one path without browsing the entire repository catalog.

sections.title: Choose the layer that owns your problem

steps.title: Use Agent Plugins for focused host guidance
steps.description: Choose a narrow plugin when Claude Code already supplies the execution loop.
steps.completion: You can choose a plugin without granting it new runtime authority.

steps.title: Use Harness for a native agent loop
steps.description: Adopt Harness when provider-neutral execution, approvals, budgets, and sessions are requirements.
steps.completion: You know when a plugin is enough and when you need a native loop.

steps.title: Inspect tools and approvals
steps.description: See how Harness separates available tools from the decisions that permit consequential effects.
steps.completion: You can identify where an approval decision is recorded and enforced.

steps.title: Run the Harness getting started path
steps.description: Complete the repository-owned first run and retain its session evidence.
steps.completion: A run completes with its decisions and effects available for inspection.

steps.title: Add a confinement boundary
steps.description: Use Substrate when commands or tools require an explicit execution boundary.
steps.completion: The execution boundary and allowed operations are explicit.

steps.title: Evaluate with Metaharness
steps.description: Drive or compare harnesses from outside their native loop when independent observation matters.
steps.completion: You can compare retained outcomes without relying only on the harness's own account.

steps.title: Read the Devcenter profile
steps.description: Separate the product proposition from its current public artifacts and deployment access.
steps.completion: You can state what is publicly inspectable and what remains gated.

sections.title: Use the credential-free public review path

steps.title: Run the frontend review without private artifacts
steps.description: Follow the source-owned frontend review workflow; the separate full-service build requires approved private dependencies.
steps.completion: The credential-free review runs locally, and your notes preserve the less-than-32-day evaluation license boundary.

steps.title: Confirm the current availability statement
steps.description: Treat private images and internal-only services as blockers to public deployment until the owning project says otherwise.
steps.completion: Your evaluation notes distinguish review access from deployability.

steps.title: Inspect declared service relationships
steps.description: Use the public architecture map to identify the service that owns the boundary you need.
steps.completion: You can name the owning service without assuming the reading order is a deployment stack.

steps.title: Operate AEP Service
steps.description: Use the source-owned service documentation for configuration, security, reliability, and operations.
steps.completion: The deployment follows an explicitly published service contract.

steps.title: Operate governed connector boundaries
steps.description: Use Connectors documentation when external actions require catalog, credentials, grants, invocation, and events.
steps.completion: External effects have an attributable, bounded operations path.

sections.title: Keep access and support claims explicit

steps.title: Check the owning project's current status
steps.description: Verify maturity, required artifacts, and access before copying any deployment command.
steps.completion: No deployment plan depends on an artifact that the public cannot obtain.

steps.title: Read the Docs System contract
steps.description: Learn which metadata, collection, validation, and shared presentation concerns belong to Docs System.
steps.completion: You can separate source truth, shared contracts, Website presentation, and Atlas delivery.

steps.title: Find the repository that owns the claim
steps.description: Use project profiles and source links to edit technical content at its authority rather than in an imported snapshot.
steps.completion: The proposed change is located in the repository that owns the technical claim.

steps.title: Preview through the canonical Website shell
steps.description: Validate collected routes, passive Markdown, assets, search metadata, and redirects with the exact source revision.
steps.completion: The source page renders correctly at its canonical root-site URL.

steps.title: Inspect changes and releases
steps.description: Confirm that the public change stream and source revision agree after publication.
steps.completion: The root site, source revision, feeds, and compatibility routes describe one release.
